decisive_items: symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6
response.rationale: Viral prodrome, diffuse ST elevation with low QRS voltage, high troponin, and normal coronary arteries are most consistent with acute myocarditis; ACS is excluded by normal angiography, and stress/takotsubo or sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy are less consistent with this age and ECG pattern.

rejected.why: Takotsubo is less likely in a young patient with viral prodrome and diffuse ST elevation/low voltage; no typical apical ballooning or emotional trigger.
Acute coronary syndrome is excluded by normal coronary arteries despite elevated troponin and ST elevation.
Stress cardiomyopathy is less likely because the infection-related myocardial inflammation and ECG findings favor myocarditis.
Sepsis explains elevated procalcitonin and shock but not the chest pain, high troponin, diffuse ST elevation, and LV wall-motion pattern as a primary cardiac process.
